title: Rituximab in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction. A phase 2 placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial.
official:
Rituximab in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction. A phase 2 placebo controlled randomized clinical trial.
RITA-MI 2
summary: Main objective: The primary objective is to compare the effect of a single injection of two doses of rituximab versus placebo on 6 months left ventricular systolic function, using CMR, in patients who have had an acute anterior STEMI or a large inferior MI.

interventions.name: MabThera 500 mg concentrate for solution for infusion

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1)	Age>18 years with no upper limit (women must be either postmenopausal defined as being amenorrhoeic for greater than 2 years with an appropriate clinical profile, e.g. age appropriate (>55 years old), history of vasomotor symptoms) or having documented hysterectomy and/or bilateral oophorectomy) ;
2. 2)	Clinical evidence at presentation of anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) involving the proximal or mid left anterior descending (LAD) defined as symptoms suggestive of acute myocardial ischemia, an electrocardiogram showing ST-segment elevation ≥2 mm in ≥2 contiguous leads in V1 to V4 or a large inferior MI (right coronary artery (RCA), or left circumflex (LCx) coronary artery) with evidence of low-ejection fraction (LVEF<45%);
3. 3)	Complete occlusion (i.e. TIMI flow 0-1) of proximal or mid left anterior descending (LAD), right coronary artery (RCA), or left circumflex (LCx) coronary artery  coronary artery on urgent angiography interpreted as the infarct-related artery (IRA); angiography interpreted as the infarct-related artery (IRA);
4. 4)	Onset of worse symptoms within 48 hours before primary PCI;
5. 5)	Patients with neutrophils >1.5 x 109/L at the moment of admission
6. 6)	Patients with platelet counts >75 x 109/L at the moment of admission
7. 7)	Plan to provide primary percutaneous angioplasty (PPCI) for the patient within 2 hours of ECG diagnosis confirmed before enrollment ;;
8. 8)	Ability to start infusion of rituximab within 3 hours of PPCI ;confirmed before enrollment ;
9. 9)	Written informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1)	History of previous myocardial infarction without documented preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF >50%) prior to the current admission will be an exclusion criterion
2. 25)	Inability to comply with study procedures
3. 26)	Patients under guardianship or curatorship
4. 10)	Active COVID-19 infection or COVID-19 infection within 3 months
5. 3)	Cardiogenic shock (defined as systolic blood pressure <90 mmHg for >30minutes, or necessitating vasopressors to achieve a blood pressure ≥90 mmHg)
6. 4)	Cardiac electrical instability (defined as complete heart block needing temporary pacing or any tachyarrhythmia needing cardioversion)
7. 6)	History of severe chronic renal failure (defined as stage 4 (GFR = 15-29 mL/min) or worse)
8. 7)	History of hepatitis B, HIV or tuberculosis
9. 8)	Patient positive for point of care bedside test of Ag HBs
10. 9)	Severe, progressive infections documented
11. 11)	Patient with documented severe immune deficiency
12. 18)	Contraindications to injectable Polaramine: o  Risk of closed-angle glaucoma, o Risk of urinary retention linked to urethro-prostatic disorders
13. 12)	Presence, or history in ≤ five years, of an ongoing cancer, (except in situ cancer of the cervix or basal cell carcinoma)
14. 13)	QTcF> 450 msecs in males, > 470msecs in females
15. 14)	Any oral or intravenous immunosuppressive treatment, immune modulatory monoclonal antibodies or immunodepleting therapy at any time (inhalers and topical creams with corticosteroids are permitted)
16. 15)	Previous history of major organ transplant including renal transplant
17. 16)	Known hypersensitivity to the active substance of rituximab or to proteins of murine origin, or to any of the other excipients
18. 17)	Any contraindications to any of the rituximab  premedication drugs
19. 5)	Patients with Killip class III heart failure
20. 19)	Expected need for vaccination with a live attenuated vaccine during the study, including incomplete vaccination courses (in case, life, attenuated vaccine must be administered at least 30 days before inclusion in study)
21. 2)	Presentation with cardiac arrest
22. 20)	Absence of a complete COVID-19 vaccination scheme (including recovery from documented COVID infection) as approved at the time of enrolment in the country where the patient is recruited
23. 21)	Any obvious contraindications for MRI or conditions which will impede image acquisition for example: o	Severe claustrophobia o	Non-MRI compatible permanent pacemaker o	Patients who have a metallic foreign body (metal silver) in their eye, or who have an aneurysm clip in their brain o	Patients who have had metallic devices placed in their back  o	Known hypersensitivity to imaging products (gadoteric acid, meglumin or any drug containing gadolinium)
24. 22)	Known hepatic failure
25. 23)	Previous history of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy
26. 24)	Inclusion in other interventional drug study within the previous 3 months
